claim: Recent language models called Large Reasoning Models generate detailed thinking processes before giving an answer.
quote: Recent generations of language models have introduced Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) that generate detailed thinking processes before providing answers.
counts_if: The retelling says reasoning models produce a long chain of thought or thinking before answering.
contradicted_if: The retelling says reasoning models answer directly without any intermediate thinking.

claim: The fundamental capabilities, scaling behavior and limitations of reasoning models are still not well understood.
quote: their fundamental capabilities, scaling properties, and limitations remain insufficiently understood
counts_if: The retelling says it is still unclear what reasoning models can fundamentally do and where they fail.
contradicted_if: The retelling says reasoning models' capabilities and limits are already fully understood.

claim: Current evaluations of reasoning models focus mainly on math and coding benchmarks and final answer accuracy.
quote: Current evaluations primarily focus on established math and coding benchmarks, emphasizing final answer accuracy.
counts_if: The retelling says models are usually tested on math and coding benchmarks judged by whether the final answer is right.
contradicted_if: The retelling says current evaluations mostly examine the reasoning steps rather than final answers or do not use math and coding benchmarks.

claim: Standard math and coding benchmark evaluations often suffer from data contamination.
quote: this evaluation paradigm often suffers from contamination and does not provide insights into the reasoning traces
counts_if: The retelling says typical benchmarks may be contaminated, for example by test material leaking into training data.
contradicted_if: The retelling says standard benchmarks are free of contamination.

claim: Standard benchmark evaluations give no insight into the models' reasoning traces.
quote: this evaluation paradigm often suffers from contamination and does not provide insights into the reasoning traces
counts_if: The retelling says ordinary benchmark scores do not reveal how the model reasoned step by step.
contradicted_if: The retelling says standard benchmarks already reveal the models' detailed reasoning traces.

claim: The authors used controllable puzzle environments in which problem complexity can be set precisely while the logical structure stays the same.
quote: we systematically investigate these gaps with the help of controllable puzzle environments that allow precise manipulation of complexity while maintaining consistent logical structures
counts_if: The retelling says the study used puzzles whose difficulty could be dialed up in controlled steps.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the study used only standard fixed math and coding benchmarks or uncontrolled real-world tasks.

claim: The puzzle setup lets the authors analyze not just final answers but also the models' internal reasoning traces.
quote: This setup enables the analysis of not only final answers but also the internal reasoning traces, offering insights into how LRMs think.
counts_if: The retelling says the study looked at the models' reasoning steps as well as their final answers.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the study looked only at final answers and not at the reasoning.

claim: Reasoning models suffer a complete collapse in accuracy once problems pass a certain level of complexity.
quote: we show that LRMs face a complete accuracy collapse beyond certain complexities
counts_if: The retelling says reasoning models' accuracy falls to essentially zero on problems beyond some difficulty.
contradicted_if: The retelling says reasoning models' accuracy declines only gradually or stays high at any complexity.

claim: Reasoning effort first rises with problem complexity, then declines past a point even though the model still has token budget left.
quote: their reasoning effort increases with problem complexity up to a point, then declines despite having remaining token budget
counts_if: The retelling says models think harder as problems get harder but then reduce their thinking on the hardest problems despite room to think more.
contradicted_if: The retelling says reasoning effort keeps increasing with complexity or that models stop only because they run out of tokens.

claim: On low-complexity tasks, standard models outperform reasoning models.
quote: By comparing LRMs with their standard LLM counterparts under same inference compute, we identify three performance regimes: (1) low-complexity tasks where standard models outperform LRMs,
counts_if: The retelling says that on easy problems regular models do better than reasoning models.
contradicted_if: The retelling says reasoning models beat standard models on easy problems.

claim: On medium-complexity tasks, reasoning models have an advantage over standard models.
quote: (2) medium-complexity tasks where LRMs demonstrates advantage, and (3) high-complexity tasks where both models face complete collapse.
counts_if: The retelling says reasoning models do better than standard models on moderately difficult problems.
contradicted_if: The retelling says standard models match or beat reasoning models on moderately difficult problems.

claim: On high-complexity tasks, both reasoning and standard models collapse completely.
quote: (2) medium-complexity tasks where LRMs demonstrates advantage, and (3) high-complexity tasks where both models face complete collapse.
counts_if: The retelling says that on the hardest problems both kinds of model fail entirely.
contradicted_if: The retelling says reasoning models still succeed on the hardest problems or that only standard models fail there.

claim: Reasoning models are limited in exact computation: they fail to use explicit algorithms and reason inconsistently across problem scales.
quote: We found that LRMs have limitations in exact computation: they fail to use explicit algorithms and reason inconsistently across scales.
counts_if: The retelling says reasoning models struggle to carry out exact step-by-step computation or to follow explicit algorithms reliably.
contradicted_if: The retelling says reasoning models reliably execute explicit algorithms and compute exactly at all scales.

claim: The authors also examined the reasoning traces in more depth, studying the patterns of solutions the models explored.
quote: We also investigate the reasoning traces in more depth, studying the patterns of explored solutions
counts_if: The retelling says the authors looked closely at the models' reasoning traces and the solution attempts within them.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the authors did not look at the reasoning traces in detail.

claim: The puzzle environments are only a narrow slice of reasoning tasks and may not capture the diversity of real-world or knowledge-intensive reasoning.
quote: they represent a narrow slice of reasoning tasks and may not capture the diversity of real-world or knowledge-intensive reasoning problems
counts_if: The retelling says the puzzles cover only a limited range of reasoning, so results may not carry over to real-world or knowledge-heavy tasks.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the puzzles represent all reasoning tasks or that the results certainly apply to real-world reasoning.

claim: The puzzle environments allow controlled experiments with fine-grained control over problem complexity.
quote: our puzzle environments enable controlled experimentation with fine-grained control over problem complexity
counts_if: The retelling says the puzzles let the authors vary difficulty finely in controlled experiments.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the authors could not control problem difficulty.

claim: Most experiments used black-box API access to closed frontier models, which limits analysis of their internal states or architecture.
quote: most of our experiments rely on black-box API access to the closed frontier LRMs, limiting our ability to mechanistically analyze internal states or architectural components
counts_if: The retelling says the authors tested closed models only through their APIs and so could not inspect model internals.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the authors had full access to model internals and analyzed the architecture or internal states.

claim: Using deterministic puzzle simulators assumes that reasoning can be perfectly validated step by step.
quote: the use of deterministic puzzle simulators assumes that reasoning can be perfectly validated step by step
counts_if: The retelling says the method relies on puzzle simulators that can check every reasoning step exactly.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the method makes no assumption about step-by-step validation of reasoning.

claim: In less structured domains such precise validation may not be possible, which limits how far the analysis transfers to open-ended reasoning.
quote: in less structured domains, such precise validation may not be feasible, limiting the transferability of this analysis to other more generalizable and open-ended reasoning
counts_if: The retelling says the analysis may not transfer to open-ended reasoning where steps cannot be checked so precisely.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the analysis transfers directly to open-ended, less structured reasoning.
